chapter: Hearing Louis and the Baton Rouge scene
title: First hearing Louis Armstrong at a Firemen's Parade
summary: At about twelve, Joe heard a young Louis with a Tuxedo brass band in Baton Rouge, and a porter in the crowd named him.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: We've got you when you went back to Baton Rouge and quit the circus. Let me just interrupt it there, and go back to something that I wanted to ask you about. You were telling me about the first time you heard Louis.
That was about...heck, I would say maybe...
So that would have been about 1918.
Something like that, or maybe I was a little older.
Where was this? Can you remember?
This was one of them Firemen Parades.

In Baton Rouge. Like I said, every parade that passed in Baton Rouge, passed in front of my house. We had a kind of a little roof on the top of my Dad's house. We lived in the... The shoe shop was in the front, and we lived in the house in the back. But anyway, I'm standing along the curb with a lot of kids, you know, watching this music go by, with different little floats and everything
there. But then in this distance, if I'm not mistaken, old Guy Kelly was standing up there. I can't think of all the guys that played.

And we heard this trumpet, this cornet. I think it might have been... It was either "That's A Plenty" or "Panama Rag." And when I heard that thing, you couldn't believe it. And everybody.... Nobody asked "Where's Louis?" in Baton Rouge. I think that was the first time he had come to Baton Rouge.
What band was it with? Do you remember?
Tuxedo Brass Band, it would have been.
But I never seen them in a tuxedo.
Sometimes when they posed for (?) the pictures.
Somebody told me how they got that name.
They played at a tuxedo dance.

Yeah. Anyway, it wasn't from wearing tuxedos, I don't believe. Anyway, these guys are, "What is that instrument? Who is playing that cornet?" I think a guy said, "It sounds like a cornet. But nobody can play

like that." So finally, as they're marching, Louis had that horn up there with that little old red hat on, just blowing up a breeze. He's got his little head up there, overpowering everybody. So when they got by, naturally we were going to light out. But before, some guy in the back of me or something, he's a railroad porter on a train, he says, "I know who that is. They call him Dipper. His name is Louis Armstrong." "I know who he is," the guy kept saying. "I know him!" In the meantime, we're gone, making that second line right behind him.
